factual_methodological.summary: Central claims remain those fact-checked against primary Fed, BoE, BOJ, ECB, IMF and NDB material in the prior QA pass. Revision 1 changes taxonomy and PT-BR localization only; figures, dates, causal qualifications, scenarios and conclusions are unchanged.

taxonomy.summary: institutional-change is a controlled phenomenon and the remaining program, series/domain, dimensions, geography and topics remain valid.

translation.summary: Previously blocking English institutional and market terms are now localized naturally in PT-BR without altering evidence status or figures.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening states the two-part institutional thesis directly; headings are mechanism-oriented; localization is natural; no prompt/template or QA meta-text is exposed; repetition is controlled and sections progress from decisions through transmission to monitoring.

contextual_depth.summary: Institutional and policy context is incorporated where needed to interpret transmission; no ornamental historical section is required.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The brief meets the visual floor. The rate chart explicitly disclaims cross-country tightness comparability and the structural flow matches the defended transmission mechanisms; EN/PT-BR evidence remains parallel.

contrary_evidence: The selected policy-rate chart compares different operating frameworks and is not evidence of relative monetary tightness; the article states this limitation.
NDB strategy and project approvals do not by themselves establish a change in the global monetary order; the article explicitly limits the inference.
limitations: The monitor combines decisions across institutions with different mandates and operating frameworks, so cross-institution comparison is mechanism-based rather than a single quantitative scale.
notes: Revision 1 resolves the prior blocking taxonomy and PT-BR localization findings. No public bundle for this ID was found at decision time.

en.title: Global Monetary Institutions — September 22, 2026
en.deck: The latest institutional cycle combines tighter policy in the United States and Japan, a divided hold in the United Kingdom, a new IMF–World Bank debt framework for low-income countries, live Eurosystem settlement of tokenised assets in central bank money, and a new NDB strategy cycle.
en.regime: Major central banks are diverging in policy implementation while multilateral institutions are changing debt assessment and settlement infrastructure.
en.key_risk: Energy-driven inflation and restrictive long-term financing can keep policy tighter even as official institutions expand new settlement and development-finance channels.

pt-BR.title: Instituições Monetárias Globais — 22 de setembro de 2026
pt-BR.deck: O ciclo institucional mais recente combina aperto monetário nos Estados Unidos e no Japão, manutenção dividida dos juros no Reino Unido, novo marco FMI–Banco Mundial para dívida de países de baixa renda, liquidação de ativos tokenizados em moeda de banco central no Eurosistema e novo ciclo estratégico do NDB.
pt-BR.regime: Grandes bancos centrais divergem na condução monetária enquanto instituições multilaterais alteram avaliação de dívida e infraestrutura de liquidação.
pt-BR.key_risk: Inflação associada à energia e financiamento de longo prazo restritivo podem manter a política monetária apertada mesmo com expansão de novos canais de liquidação e financiamento multilateral.
